message:
fix(check): pin @types/node and resolve it through the configured registry (#36883)

`deno check` installs `@types/node` for projects that don't bring their
own (`ensure_types_node`). That download had two problems:

- it fetched the packument from a hardcoded
`https://registry.npmjs.org`, ignoring the registry the project
configured (`.npmrc`, `NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY`);
- with no version requirement it took whatever `dist-tags.latest`
pointed at.

So type checking wasn't reproducible: the same code on the same commit
can produce different diagnostics depending on when you run it, a
private-registry or offline setup isn't honored, and our own spec tests
reach live npm despite the test harness pointing them at the local
registry. A DefinitelyTyped release then changes diagnostics for
everyone — it has repeatedly broken `check_node_builtin_modules`
(#36711, #36848, and again now, which blocks CI on every PR).

This resolves the package through the configured registry and pins the
version to the one `cli/tsc/dts/node` is generated from, so the
downloaded typings match the built-in ones. `tools/update_types_node.ts`
reads the pin from the Rust constant, so bumping is one edit plus a
regen.

One subtlety: a materialized copy was reused whenever it was complete,
so a tree left by an older Deno (installed back when this followed
`latest`) would be type-checked against forever. Reuse now requires the
pinned version, and the extractor's "another process published this
first" race check compares versions too, so a wrong-version tree is
replaced rather than kept.

A project that wants different Node typings still wins by installing its
own `@types/node` under `node_modules`; that branch is unchanged.

Verified locally: `check_node_builtin_modules` passes against the
**unchanged** expectation files, resolving 24.2.0 from the vendored test
registry rather than live npm. All 270 `check` specs, the `sync_types`
spec and the `npm_compat` unit tests pass. Two new unit tests cover
replacing a wrong-version tree and keeping a matching one.

Supersedes #36882, which just updated the expectation to today's
`@types/node` output — a fix that would drift again on the next release.

### Also: timezone-dependent `node_test_mock_timers` (second commit)

Folded in from #36884 because the two unblock CI together: each needs
the other for a reliably green run.

`Date is mocked and tracks tick` mocks the clock at 5000 ms past the
epoch and asserted that `Date()` matches `/1970/`. `Date()` formats in
local time, so west of UTC that instant is 31 December 1969. It failed
on a windows-aarch64 runner in Pacific time, and because it threw before
`mock.timers.reset()` the next seven tests failed too. It now compares
against `new Date(5000).toString()`, which is exact in any timezone.
Reproduced with `TZ=America/Los_Angeles`; the fixed file passes under
`UTC`, `America/Los_Angeles`, `Etc/GMT+12` and `Pacific/Kiritimati`.
